nodes.title: Base prompt: black & white
widgets_values: Create a complete black and white manga illustration of the character from <image1>, placed in a detailed, fully drawn background scene that fits her outfit, pose and mood, such as a street, a classroom, a room, a park or a shop, drawn in the same ink and screentone style. The background fills the whole frame from edge to edge; there is no white or empty area. Show more of the character than <image1> does, extending the framing naturally downwards and to the sides, as the original illustration she was cropped from would. Keep exactly her face, expression, hairstyle, outfit, pose of the visible part, line art, ink and screentone style. Draw the missing parts of her body consistent with the visible ones. No text, no sound effects, no speech bubbles, no panel borders.

- 怎么补:D6 社区件标缺;下载模型逐件请示(D7),装插件另行明令(D6)。

# Manga page → character illustrations

Detects every character on a manga page, crops each one and redraws it with **Qwen Image 2.1** as a complete illustration with a background, extending the framing naturally and completing what the panel hides.

## How to use
1. **Manga page**: load the page (or a single panel).
2. **Detection**
   - *full page (true)*: best when characters break panel borders or fill the page.
   - *per panel (false)*: best for small characters, each one inside its own panel.
3. **Characters to find**: SAM3 text prompt, max 32 tokens. `:N` is the maximum detections **per prompt and per image** (per panel in per-panel mode).
   - `anime character:8` → everyone
   - `anime character:1` → the main one in each panel
   - `blonde girl:1, girl with long black hair:1` → specific characters
4. **Detection threshold**: raise it (0.6–0.7) to drop background people and slivers; lower it if small characters are missed.
5. **Redraw**: *characters (true)* redraws each character; *whole panels (false)* redraws each panel.
6. **Redraw style**: pick `color` or `black_and_white`. The matching **Base prompt** always asks for a full background and a natural, wider framing (not forced full body). Refer to the crop as `<image1>`.
7. **Prompt upsampler** (off by default): off keeps the redraw closest to the original drawing, with softer colors. On, Qwen3-VL 8B looks at each crop and rewrites the base prompt for it: viewpoint (front / profile / from behind), a color for every element that matches the manga values (solid black hair stays dark, white hair becomes blonde), knee-up or full-body framing, clothing for the hidden lower body, a specific background scene, and removal of sound effects. Its output is shown in **Upsampled prompt** inside Redraw; edit **Upsampler system prompt** there to change the rules. Off uses the base prompt as is: faster and more faithful, with weaker colors, and sound effects or back views are handled less reliably.
   **Character notes**: optional, one line per character, starting with how to recognize them, e.g. `Girl with long black hair: maid, black dress, white apron` or `Blonde boy with glasses: student, gakuran uniform`. The upsampler applies the line that matches each crop (role, colors, clothing) and ignores the rest; leave it empty to let it decide. With the upsampler off, the notes are appended to the base prompt as is, so keep them to the character(s) on this page; with several characters the model may mix their attributes.
   **Output canvas**: *custom size (true)* computes the canvas from each crop: crop aspect ratio × **Canvas expand** (width ×, height ×) at **Canvas megapixels**, rounded to multiples of 32. Expand 1 / 1 keeps the crop's exact aspect; e.g. height × 1.3 leaves 30 % more room below to complete the figure. Keep megapixels around 1 (Qwen Image 2.1 supports up to ~4). *crop size (false)* uses the crop's own size, better for whole panels.
8. Run. Crops are saved to `output/manga_chars/crop_*`, illustrations to `output/manga_chars/`.

## Tips
- Every crop runs through the rest of the graph once; mute (Ctrl+M) **Redraw** to check detections quickly.
- Balloons and text are whitened before detection. Hand-drawn sound effects are not detected; the prompt asks Qwen to remove them (more reliable with the upsampler).
- The upsampler picks colors per crop, so the same character can get different colors in different panels. For consistency, describe each character's colors in **Character notes**.
- Each character takes about 9 s with the upsampler off and about 25 s with it on (6 steps on this engine).
- In per-panel mode every panel needs at least one detected character.
- Engine settings (padding, crop size, sampler) live inside the subgraphs in the **Engine** group; models and the turbo LoRA are loaded in **Qwen Image 2.1 models**.
- No Bria/Fibo (CC BY-NC 4.0) model is used in this version.

## Required custom nodes
Install with ComfyUI-Manager (search by name) or `git clone` into `custom_nodes/`. Requires ComfyUI **v0.42.0+** (core SAM3 and Qwen Image 2.1 nodes).

| Package | Nodes used |
|---|---|
| [ComfyUI Impact Pack](https://github.com/ltdrdata/ComfyUI-Impact-Pack) | SegmDetectorSEGS, SegsToCombinedMask, ImpactSEGSNMSFilter, ImpactSEGSToMaskList, MasksToMaskList, ImpactImageBatchToImageList |
| [ComfyUI Impact Subpack](https://github.com/ltdrdata/ComfyUI-Impact-Subpack) | UltralyticsDetectorProvider |
| [KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes) | GrowMaskWithBlur, GetMaskSizeAndCount, ImageCropByMaskAndResize, ImagePadKJ, LazySwitchKJ |
| [comfyui-obvpm](https://github.com/chanon/comfyui-obvpm) | LazyCaseSwitch |
| [comfyui_api_executor_nodes](https://github.com/quinteroac/comfyui_api_executor_nodes) | SimpleText (the two redraw prompts) |

Everything else is ComfyUI core.

## Models
- `checkpoints/sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors`
- `ultralytics/segm/manga_panel.pt` (frame / text / balloon)
- `diffusion_models/qwen_image_2.1_int8_convrot.safetensors` + `loras/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo-v0.3-6step-lora-r256.safetensors`
- `text_encoders/qwen3vl_8b_bf16_heretic.safetensors`
- `vae/qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors`

## Local engine adaptation (MYStudio Win engine, 1124)
- Model files above point to this engine's inventory (names differ from the author's layout).
- Redraw steps are fixed at **6** for the v0.3 6-step turbo LoRA.
- `manga_panel.pt` was never published by the author: **Clean page & split panels is muted** and detection reads the raw page directly. Balloons are not whitened before detection, and per-panel mode is unavailable. Unmute the subgraph after installing the weight.
- **Upsampled prompt** now reads the LazySwitchKJ output, so the Qwen3-VL upsampler only runs when enabled (preview shows the prompt actually used).

nodes.title: Upsampler system prompt
widgets_values: You write prompts for an image-editing model. It receives <image1>, a character cropped from a manga page on a white background, and the user's base instruction. Rewrite the base instruction into ONE detailed English prompt, a single prose paragraph with no lists or markdown, that keeps every requirement of the base instruction (color or black and white, background, framing) and starts with "Create a complete". 1) State the viewpoint exactly as seen: facing the viewer, in profile, or seen from behind (if only the back of the head is visible, say the character is seen from behind and the face is not visible). 2) Describe the visible hair, face, expression and outfit. If the base instruction asks for color, assign a specific color to every element, agreeing with the manga values: hair filled with solid black is black or very dark brown; hair left white or only outlined is blonde, platinum or very light; gray screentone areas are mid-tone colors; white areas stay white or very light. Give clothing plausible saturated colors such as navy, burgundy, beige or forest green, never plain gray. If the base instruction asks for black and white, describe ink, screentone and gray values instead of colors. The base instruction may end with character notes from the user, one per line, each starting with how to recognize a character. Match a note to <image1> only by checking its recognizable details against the image: hair value first (hair filled with solid black ink is dark hair; hair left white or only outlined is blonde or light hair), then hair length and style, clothing and props. A note about dark hair never matches a character with white or outlined hair, and a note about blonde or light hair never matches a character with solid black hair. If exactly one note matches, follow its role, colors and clothing, overriding your own choices; if no note clearly matches, ignore all notes. Never mention the notes themselves. 3) Ask to keep exactly the face, expression, hairstyle, outfit, pose and line art of <image1>. 4) Framing: never a close-up, portrait or bust shot. Use a knee-up or a full-body shot, whichever fits the visible pose, and list the body parts that must be drawn below the crop. If the lower clothing is not visible, dress the lower body consistently with the visible outfit (matching skirt or trousers, socks and shoes); never leave the legs bare unless they are bare in <image1>. 5) Invent one specific, detailed background scene that suits the character, in the requested style, filling the whole frame with no white areas. 6) If <image1> contains sound effects or lettering, say they must be removed. End with: No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders.
